This tutorial makes one orthomosaic per date for all the drone flights of a site, from a few dates to several
hundreds, with `generate_mosaics()`. It assumes canobsR is installed (`vignette("Installation-guide")`).

## The method in two sentences

**Time-SIFT** ([Feurer & Vinatier 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2018.10.016)) computes the camera
positions of several dates **together**, in one photogrammetric block: the mosaics of these dates are then
consistent with each other, without ground control points. A block of 100 dates would not fit in memory, so the
dates are processed by **chunks** of about ten dates; the small shifts left between chunks are corrected afterwards
by `align_mosaics()` (`vignette("Align-orthomosaics")`), and `aggregate_mosaics()` makes light 50 cm
versions with spectral indices (`vignette("Aggregate-mosaics")`).

## 1. Organise the flights

canobsR finds the date and the drone of each flight **in the name of its folder**: this is the only convention
to follow. A site is organised as follows (the folders after `1_flights` are made by canobsR; the names are
suggestions):

```
D:/bouamir/                          one folder per site
  1_flights/                         flights_dir: one subfolder per flight
    RGB_20220427/                    <prefix>_<YYYYMMDD>: flight of the main drone of the site
      DJI_0001.JPG ...               images (subfolders allowed)
    RGB_20220511/
    RGB_20220525/
    RGB_20220525_Matrice4E/          <prefix>_<YYYYMMDD>_<drone>: flight of another drone
    notes/                           no date in the name: ignored
  2_mosaics/                         out_dir of generate_mosaics()
    orthomosaics/                    20220427.tif, 20220511.tif, ..., 20220525_Matrice4E.tif
    plan.csv, journal.csv, logs/ ...
  3_aligned/                         out_dir of align_mosaics()
  4_mosaics_50cm/                    out_dir of aggregate_mosaics()
```

Rules of the flight folder names:

* **Date**: `YYYYMMDD` (or `YYYYMM` for monthly series) anywhere in the name; the prefix (`RGB`, `MS`, the site
  name...) is free. The date of the folder is the date of the mosaic, whatever the EXIF dates of the images (a
  flight interrupted by rain and finished the next day stays one mosaic).
* **Drone**: what follows the date names the drone (`_Matrice4E`, `_M3T`...). **No suffix = the main drone of the
  site** (for example the Mavic 2 Pro used since the start of the series): there is nothing to rename in an
  existing series. Each date and drone gives one mosaic, named `<date>[_<drone>]`: two drones flown the same day
  give `20220525.tif` and `20220525_Matrice4E.tif`.
* One folder per flight. Two folders with the same date and drone (e.g. a site flown in two parts) make one mosaic.
* Avoid spaces and accents in the paths (some photogrammetry tools fail with them).

## 2. Check the flights

```{r}
library(canobsR)
flights_dir <- "D:/bouamir/1_flights"
chk <- check_flights(flights_dir)
chk$folders[chk$folders$status != "ok", ]
```

`check_flights()` reads the EXIF of all the images and points out, per folder, images taken on another day than the
folder date, images without GPS position, and images found twice (in two folders, for example). It changes nothing.

## 3. Make the mosaics

```{r}
out_dir <- "D:/bouamir/2_mosaics"
generate_mosaics(flights_dir, out_dir)
```

That is all. With the default settings:

| Setting | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `engine` | `"odm"` | OpenDroneMap; `"metashape"` with a Metashape licence |
| `resolution` | `0.05` | pixel size, metres |
| `crs` | `"auto"` | UTM zone of the site, from the GPS positions of the images (e.g. EPSG:32633) |
| `keep_dem` | `FALSE` | `TRUE` also saves the elevation models in `out_dir/dem` |
| `tmp_dir` | `out_dir/_tmp` | temporary files (tens of GB for large sites): put it on a disk with space |
| `n_cores` | `"auto"` | threads of ODM: processors minus a few, limited by the memory (see below) |

What it prints:

```
====================================================================================================
generate_mosaics(): D:/bouamir/1_flights
  -> D:/bouamir/2_mosaics
====================================================================================================
crs: EPSG:32633 (WGS 84 / UTM zone 33N), from the GPS positions of 312 images (median lat 3.21, lon 13.05)
engine odm, 0.05 m, EPSG:32633
104 dates (31950 images) in 11 chunks; plan: D:/bouamir/2_mosaics/plan.csv
  main drone: 98 dates, 30127 images, 10 chunk(s)
  Matrice4E: 6 dates, 1823 images, 1 chunk(s)
  dates per chunk: 6 to 10
0/104 mosaics already made; 11 chunk(s) to process
====================================================================================================
[##########--------------------] 4/11 chunks   chunk_005: 10 dates, 3104 images (main drone)   remaining time: 31.5 h
====================================================================================================
  ... (ODM steps)
[OK] chunk_005: 10 mosaic(s) in 4.4 h
```

and a report at the end. The results, in `out_dir`:

```
orthomosaics/   20220427.tif, 20220511.tif, ..., 20220525_Matrice4E.tif
dem/            (keep_dem = TRUE)
plan.csv        chunks of dates
journal.csv     one row per mosaic: chunk, status (done / failed), time, error message
settings.json   settings of the series (engine, resolution, crs, ...)
logs/           full output of each chunk
```

## 4. Interruptions, errors, new flights: run the same command again

```{r}
generate_mosaics(flights_dir, out_dir)
```

* **After an interruption** (crash, power cut, Esc, computer needed for something else): the mosaics already made
  are skipped (`journal.csv`), and an interrupted chunk restarts from its last finished step (its project was kept).
* **After errors**: a chunk that fails is recorded with its error, and the next chunk starts. Running the command
  again retries the failed chunks only. `on_error = "stop"` stops at the first error instead.
* **New flights**: add their folders and run the command again: they are planned in new chunks, and only they are
  processed.

The settings of the series (resolution, crs, ...) are saved at the first run; a later run with other settings warns
that the mosaics already made keep the previous ones (`overwrite = TRUE` makes them again).

## 5. The plan of chunks

`generate_mosaics()` makes the plan itself, with `plan_mosaics()`, the first time. To look at it, or change it,
before processing:

```{r}
plan <- plan_mosaics(flights_dir, out_dir, chunk_size = 8)
table(plan$chunk, plan$drone)
```

* **One drone per chunk** by default: different cameras in one block degrade the colour calibration and the
  matching. `split_drones = FALSE` allows mixed chunks (with a warning).
* **Random order** by default (`order = "random"`, reproducible with `seed`): each chunk mixes dates of all the
  seasons and years of the series, so all the chunks face the same variety of conditions.
  `order = "chronological"` makes chunks of consecutive dates.
* `plan.csv` can be edited by hand (column `chunk`), as long as no mosaic of the chunks concerned was made.

## 6. Large sites on one computer

* **Disk space**: the images are never copied by default. ODM needs them in its project folder: they are
  *hard-linked* there (no disk space used) when the project folder (`out_dir/projects`, or the option
  `project_dir`) is **on the same disk as the images**; otherwise they are copied, one chunk at a time. Each project
  (tens of GB) is deleted once its mosaics are made (`keep_projects = TRUE` keeps them).
* **Images on a network drive**: ODM reads each image several times; `stage_dir = "E:/stage"` copies the images of
  each chunk to a local disk before processing it, and deletes them afterwards.
* **Processors and memory**: with `n_cores = "auto"`, ODM uses the processors minus a few left free for the
  computer, within the memory available (85 % of the RAM free at the start, at most 75 % of the RAM; option
  `max_memory_gb`). Two values are used, as measured on a laptop with 28 processors and 34 GB: the alignment of the
  chunk (SfM) needs about 1.3 GB per thread for the feature detection (with 18 GB free: 11 threads; more threads
  saturated the RAM and froze the computer), while the processing of each date (dense matching, meshing) uses
  the same memory whatever the threads (all usable processors: 25). The choices are printed
  (`ODM threads, SfM block: ...`, `ODM threads, epochs: ...`). **Close the heavy programs** (browser, other
  sessions) before a long run: their memory is not available to ODM. After the SfM of a chunk, its dates are
  independent: on a computer with enough memory, several are processed at the same time (option
  `parallel_epochs`, "auto": about 3 GB + 0.27 GB per image of the largest date each; 1 on a laptop with 34 GB, 3-4
  on a server with 100 GB), which uses the GPU and the processors much better (each date alone leaves them idle
  half of the time). If the dense matching
  still runs out of memory (GPU memory of a laptop, for instance), the date is automatically processed again on the
  processor with half of the threads (same result, slower). Further options: `n_cores = 8`, or
  `downscale_factor_depth_map = 4` (depth maps at 1/4 of the image size: 0.5 GB per thread, less detailed surface),
  or fewer dates per chunk (`chunk_size = 6`; for a new plan: `plan_mosaics(..., overwrite = TRUE)`).
* **Time**: indicatively, 3 dates (133 images, 45 ha) in one chunk take 45 to 60 min with ODM on a laptop with an
  NVIDIA GPU (28 processors, 34 GB), in "Best performance" mode: about 2 h in energy saver mode. Without an NVIDIA
  GPU, the dense matching is 3 to 4 times slower.
* **Some chunks only**: `chunks = c("chunk_001", "chunk_002")`, for example to share the work between computers
  (same `out_dir` on a shared disk is not advised: give each computer its own `out_dir`).

## 7. Engines and advanced options

`engine = "odm"` (default) is free and runs on Windows, Linux (docker or native) and macOS (docker).
`engine = "metashape"` needs a licence (`canobs_install_metashape()`). Both chains are set to give comparable
results: same Time-SIFT logic, colour calibration of the images on the tie points of the block (white balance per
image, vignetting per camera), same resolution and projection. Their differences are documented in
`system.file("ENGINES.md", package = "canobsR")`.

The other settings are advanced options of `generate_mosaics()`, documented in `?generate_mosaics`, for example:

```{r}
generate_mosaics(flights_dir, out_dir, keep_dem = TRUE, tmp_dir = "E:/tmp",
                 chunk_size = 8, keypoint_limit = 20000, calibrate_col_by = "date")
```

A misspelt option is an error, not silently ignored. `generate_Mosa()` processes a single chunk (the folders given
in `folder_names`) and is what `generate_mosaics()` runs for each chunk.
